title: HDCP 2.3 transmitter (educational slice): AKE, pairing, locality check and session key exchange with a receiver over message channels, then AES-128-CTR encryption of the pixel stream

words.name: CTRL
words.desc: write: bit 0 start a session (from IDLE or AUTH; ignored while authenticating), bit 2 clear the error flags (an error in the same clock wins); reads 0

words.name: HSTATUS
words.desc: [0] busy, [1] authenticated, [2] encryption active, [3] last session failed, [4] the peer is a repeater, [5] keystream exhausted (read only)

words.name: ERR
words.desc: error flags: [0] locality timeout, [1] pairing ack mismatch, [2] locality mismatch, [3] unexpected message type, [4] message timeout, [5] keystream exhausted (read only; cleared by CTRL bit 2 or a new session)

words.name: KMIDX
words.desc: [3:0] byte index for KMDAT and KSDAT

words.name: STATE
words.desc: [3:0] authentication state: 0 IDLE, 1 AKE_INIT, 2 AKE_CERT, 3 PAIR_TX, 4 PAIR_RX, 5 LC_TX, 6 LC_WAIT, 7 SKE_TX, 8 RPT_WAIT, 9 AUTH (read only)

words.name: KSDAT
words.desc: session key ks byte KMIDX (read only)

regs.name: TXM
regs.desc: Message to the receiver; reading the type word frees it and lets the core go on

fdesc.txm_type: message type: 2 AKE_Init, 4 AKE_No_Stored_km (E_km), 9 LC_Init, 11 SKE_Send_Eks

regs.name: RXM
regs.desc: Message from the receiver; writing the type word sends it, and it is taken when the core waits for a message

fdesc.rxm_type: message type: 3 AKE_Send_Cert, 7 pairing ack, 10 LC_Send_L_prime, 12 repeater ack

irqs.name: ERROR
irqs.desc: an ERR flag is set; level in the core, so the bit is set again on every clock until CTRL bit 2 clears the flags

notes: pix_valid / pix_ready / pix_data (plain pixel words in) and enc_valid / enc_ready / enc_data (encrypted words out) pass through unchanged; words flow only while authenticated.
The core's 8-bit register window sits at REGS: each word is one core register, and only bits [7:0] are used. KMDAT is written byte by byte with KMIDX before CTRL.start.

The locality check allows 20 clocks from LC_Init to the answer: read TXM words 0, 1 and the type word, then write RXM words 0, 1 and the type word back to back (RXM words 2 and 3 can be written in advance).
